This introductory overview describes a fictional urban transport system and establishes the background for a detailed evaluation of its changing vehicle fleet.
Electric buses eliminate local tailpipe emissions while carrying passengers along established routes throughout the city every weekday.
Depot charging infrastructure requires sufficient electrical capacity and careful coordination with local utilities before new vehicles enter passenger service.
Operators should budget for staff training and maintenance equipment as well as the vehicles themselves when preparing procurement plans.
This final overview summarizes the evaluation process and reminds readers that the fictional example does not represent actual procurement advice for any particular city.
